desc: Prove the equivalence: cell (x,y) black iff y <= r[x]; column y is a top-prefix of black iff r is non-increasing; show both directions rigorously (define c[y] = #{x: r[x] >= y}, check column y black cells are exactly x <= c[y]).
Derive per-row constraints: for each row x with precolored cells, L[x] = max(Y_i) over B cells in row x (0 if none), U[x] = min(Y_i)-1 over W cells (N if none); answer No immediately if L[x] > U[x].

Implement the greedy sweep over x = 1..N using only constrained rows (M up to 2e5, N up to 1e9): sort constrained rows by x; maintain b = current max feasible value (upper end of feasible interval); for each constrained row x, feasible requires L[x] <= min(U[x], b); update b = min(U[x], b); unconstrained rows don't shrink b (U=N keeps b same, L=0 fine) — verify skipping unconstrained rows is valid.
Edge cases: rows where W cell at column 1 forces U=0; B at column N forces L=N; N=1; confirm sample 2 gives No (row1: U=1, row2: L=2 -> need r2 <= r1 <= 1 but L=2, infeasible).
Write final Python solution: read input, aggregate per-row L/U with dicts, sort rows, sweep, print Yes/No; test against all four samples mentally or by reasoning.
